questions.q: Based on the antenna pattern visual model shown (MVC-G24457614) displaying a rational function \(r(x) = \dfrac{a}{x - h} + c\) with dashed vertical asymptote \(x = h\) and horizontal asymptote \(y = c\). Compute \(h + c\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. Reading the dashed asymptotes on the graph gives vertical asymptote \(x = 3 \implies h = 3\) and horizontal asymptote \(y = 5 \implies c = 5\), so \(h + c = 8\).
questions.explain: Reading the dashed asymptotes on the graph gives vertical asymptote \(x = 3 \implies h = 3\) and horizontal asymptote \(y = 5 \implies c = 5\), so \(h + c = 8\).

questions.q: Referring to the field geometry figure (MVC-G41235219) displaying the slope field for \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1(x - y)\) and highlighted point \(P\). Evaluate the segment slope at \(P\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** D. At highlighted coordinates \((1, 3)\), \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 1(1 - 3) = -2\).

questions.q: An engineering team logged seismology measurements in the accompanying table (MVC-108344695); using these data, listing selected values of a smooth function \(f(x, y)\). Using a central difference quotient with \(\Delta x = 2\), estimate \(\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}(2, y_0)\).
questions.answer: **Answer:** A. Central difference along \(y = y_0\): \(\frac{f(3, y_0) - f(1, y_0)}{(3) - (1)} = \frac{11 - 3}{2} = 4\).
questions.explain: Central difference along \(y = y_0\): \(\frac{f(3, y_0) - f(1, y_0)}{(3) - (1)} = \frac{11 - 3}{2} = 4\).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y e^{x}, e^{x} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 2, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 1, \  -1\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=y e^{x} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 1, \  -1\right)-f\left( 2, \  0\right)=- e \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y^{2} + 1, 2 x y \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 0, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( -2, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x y^{2} + x \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -2, \  3\right)-f\left( 0, \  0\right)=-20 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y, x + z, y \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  2, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( -1, \  -1, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x y + y z \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -1, \  -1, \  3\right)-f\left( 1, \  2, \  0\right)=-4 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x + y, x + 3 y^{2} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( -1, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 0, \  -2\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x^{2} + x y + y^{3} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 0, \  -2\right)-f\left( -1, \  0\right)=-9 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x y, x^{2} - 2 \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( -2, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 1, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x^{2} y - 2 y \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 1, \  3\right)-f\left( -2, \  0\right)=-3 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x + y, x + 3 y^{2} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( -2, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 0, \  0\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x^{2} + x y + y^{3} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 0, \  0\right)-f\left( -2, \  0\right)=-4 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x + 3 y, 3 x + 3 y^{2} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  -1\right) \) to \( \left( 2, \  -2\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x^{2} + 3 x y + y^{3} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 2, \  -2\right)-f\left( 1, \  -1\right)=-13 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y, x + z, y \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  0, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( -2, \  2, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x y + y z \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -2, \  2, \  3\right)-f\left( 1, \  0, \  0\right)=2 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y^{2} + 1, 2 x y \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 2, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x y^{2} + x \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 2, \  3\right)-f\left( 1, \  0\right)=19 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x + 2 y, 2 x + 3 y^{2} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  -1\right) \) to \( \left( -2, \  1\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x^{2} + 2 x y + y^{3} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -2, \  1\right)-f\left( 1, \  -1\right)=3 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y \cos{\left(x \right)} + 1, \sin{\left(x \right)} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( -2, \  1\right) \) to \( \left( 0, \  -2\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x + y \sin{\left(x \right)} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 0, \  -2\right)-f\left( -2, \  1\right)=\sin{\left(2 \right)} + 2 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y \cos{\left(x \right)} + 1, \sin{\left(x \right)} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( -2, \  -1\right) \) to \( \left( -2, \  1\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x + y \sin{\left(x \right)} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -2, \  1\right)-f\left( -2, \  -1\right)=- 2 \sin{\left(2 \right)} \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x + 3 y, 3 x + 3 y^{2} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  2\right) \) to \( \left( -1, \  0\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x^{2} + 3 x y + y^{3} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -1, \  0\right)-f\left( 1, \  2\right)=-14 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y^{2} + 1, 2 x y \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  -1\right) \) to \( \left( 3, \  2\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x y^{2} + x \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 3, \  2\right)-f\left( 1, \  -1\right)=13 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle 2 x y, x^{2} - 2 \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 1, \  0\right) \) to \( \left( 2, \  -2\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x^{2} y - 2 y \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( 2, \  -2\right)-f\left( 1, \  0\right)=-4 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y, x + z, y \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 0, \  -2, \  1\right) \) to \( \left( -2, \  0, \  2\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x y + y z \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -2, \  0, \  2\right)-f\left( 0, \  -2, \  1\right)=2 \).

questions.q: \( \mathbf F=\langle y \cos{\left(x \right)} + 1, \sin{\left(x \right)} \rangle \) is conservative. Evaluate \( \int_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r \) along any path from \( \left( 0, \  2\right) \) to \( \left( -2, \  3\right) \).
questions.answer: A potential is \( f=x + y \sin{\left(x \right)} \). By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals the value is \( f\left( -2, \  3\right)-f\left( 0, \  2\right)=- 3 \sin{\left(2 \right)} - 2 \).
